purpose: Route sourced portfolio news into the reusable components of the news report. The output is a NewsBriefing object, not JSX or arbitrary layout instructions.

implementation.status: The reference page now renders from component props. The backend still needs to validate and supply its own payload.

routing_order: Extract atomic facts with their source article IDs and the holdings they affect. Do not generate presentation copy yet.
Group multiple articles about the same underlying event into one development. Article count is not development count.
Rank holding developments by portfolio relevance, novelty, materiality and evidence strength. Pick one lead story per affected holding.
Route forward-looking observations to NextSignals only when the source supports a concrete observable signal and its implication. Do not turn a possibility into a prediction.
Create a theme only when it connects at least two distinct holdings or developments and explains the connection; otherwise keep the fact in its holding story.
Select source articles that substantiate the displayed claims. Preserve publisher and publication time. Keep total article count separate from the selected-source count.
Write the hero last, from the ranked developments. If sentiment counts are unavailable, omit NewsSentiment instead of estimating them.

rules: Hero and developments are required to produce this report. Reject or defer a payload without a substantiated lead development.
Omit an optional section when its array is empty. Do not add filler text or a zero state to make every report look identical.
A fact may support several sections, but its full explanation should live in one place. Other sections should add a new angle instead of repeating the same paragraph.
Do not reorder sections for visual variety. Vary their contents by selecting only warranted components.
Section titles and order are renderer-owned defaults; the LLM supplies content, not new section names or arbitrary component identifiers.

sections.title: Today’s readout
sections.answers: What is the one point the reader should take away from this briefing?
rejects: sentiment inferred from only selected sources

sections.title: What matters most
sections.render_when: At least one affected holding has a sourced development.
sections.answers: Which holding is affected, what happened, and why is it relevant to this portfolio?
rejects: a story with no portfolio connection

sections.title: What happens next
sections.render_when: At least one nextSignal has both an observable signal and a sourced reason it matters.
sections.answers: What would clarify the story after this briefing?

sections.title: Themes in motion
sections.render_when: At least one cross-holding theme can explain a connection beyond shared keywords.
sections.answers: How do separate holdings and developments connect?
rejects: summed article counts presented as unique when articles overlap

sections.title: Sources & coverage
sections.render_when: At least one displayable article has title, publisher and publication time.
rejects: a selected-source count labeled as the total article count

components.answers: What dominates the readout and what context makes it matter?
rules: One synthesis headline, not a concatenation of article titles.
Summary distinguishes verified events from interpretation.
Use a report date and market session supported by the briefing metadata.

components.answers: How are classified news signals distributed?
rules: Counts are nonnegative integers drawn from the full classified signal set.
The summary and headline must agree with the counts.
Do not infer counts from the four selected sources.
Omit when no classified signal set exists.

components.answers: What is the lead news for each affected holding?
rules: One card per holding; rank cards by relevance to the portfolio.
Exposure comes from portfolio data, not the news articles.
Category is the story topic; relevance is portfolio impact; tone is news direction. Do not conflate them.
Group secondary developments in updates only when they add new information.
Use positive, negative or neutral tone; the signal wording must agree with it.
Send watch points through nextSignals and article metadata through sources, not as unused fields on a holding card.

components.answers: What evidence should the reader watch for next, and why?
rules: Ticker must exist in holdings.
Signal must be observable, such as a decision, release, filing, adoption measure or dated event.
whyItMatters explains the possible interpretation without claiming an outcome.

components.answers: What relationship links distinct holding stories?
rules: Use icon network, legal or trend as a rendering hint; never emit a component or SVG name.
Every ticker must exist in holdings and a theme normally spans at least two tickers.
The body must explain the connection, not merely repeat article headlines.
Counts may overlap across themes; disclose overlap when present.

components.answers: Where can the reader inspect the selected evidence?
rules: IDs are unique and stable within the briefing.
URL is optional; if present it must point to the article.
Publication time and publisher come from source metadata, not generated prose.
articleCount is the total analyzed; sources.length is the selected coverage count.

structural_components.rule: Wraps each conditional body with the fixed title and subtitle. The LLM does not select this component directly.

output_contract.empty_section_behavior: Omit the optional property or supply an empty array; the renderer hides that section.
output_contract.no_match_behavior: Keep the fact in the evidence record for review. Do not force it into an unrelated component or invent a new component ID.
